# Vendor patches (re-apply on every upgrade)

Every hunk is marked `// sigwin patch: <why>` in the source; search for "sigwin patch". A missed hunk fails silently (cargo warns "patch was not used"). Rules for adding or removing hunks are in `CLAUDE.md` ("Vendor patches: last resort").

## `vendor/libsignal-service`
Same rev presage pins, wired via `[patch."https://github.com/whisperfish/libsignal-service-rs"]`. Re-vendor at the new rev when bumping presage.
Its own unit tests can't run from our workspace (a patched non-member with dev-dependencies). Copy the crate out, append `[workspace]` to its `Cargo.toml`, and run `cargo test --lib` there with a short `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (boring-sys's CMake build fails on long paths). Set `LIBCLANG_PATH` as `.cargo/config.toml` does.
- `send_message_to_group` sends to up to `GROUP_SEND_CONCURRENCY` (16) members at once; upstream awaited them one by one (members x RTT).
- **Session lock**: `cipher.rs` adds `SESSION_LOCK`, taken in `ServiceCipher::decrypt` and `encrypt` (now `pub`, for the test) and around both `process_prekey_bundle` calls in `sender.rs`. libsignal loads a session, awaits the store, then saves it, with nothing stopping another task from overlapping. A receive overlapping a send lost the send's update and the peer couldn't read our next message ("invalid Whisper message", shown there as an undeliverable message); two sends reused a counter, so one message key. Upstream bug. `tests/session_lock.rs` fails if this hunk is missed.
- **Contact sync parsing**: `receiver.rs` `DeviceContactsIterator::next` (+ `ParseContactError::Truncated` in `models.rs`). A contact whose avatar length ran past the end of the decrypted list panicked in `copy_to_bytes`; with `panic = "abort"` that closed the app right after linking and lost the contact sync. Now the list ends with `Truncated`, keeping the contacts read so far (presage skips `Err`s). Also strips the attachment padding to `AttachmentPointer.size`, as Signal-Desktop does. Upstream bug; this is upstream PR whisperfish/libsignal-service-rs#483 as is (competing: #500). Drop the hunk once presage pins a rev with either. Unit tests in `receiver.rs` `mod tests`.

- **Linked device keeps the account's settings**: `websocket/account.rs` `set_account_attributes` sends only the capabilities (`PUT /v1/devices/capabilities`, new `set_device_capabilities`). presage sends the account attributes on every connect, and the server applies their registration lock, discoverability and access key to the whole account: each connect cleared the registration lock, undid "find me by number: nobody" and reverted a device rename made on the phone. Signal-Desktop, linked, sends only its capabilities. Upstream: whisperfish/presage#503 with whisperfish/libsignal-service-rs#503 (whose `set_device_capabilities` this copies). Drop the hunk once presage pins a rev with #503.

## `vendor/i-slint-renderer-software` (Slint 1.19.0, via `[patch.crates-io]`)
Re-vendor the matching version together with `i-slint-core` when upgrading Slint, then re-apply. A three-way merge does most of it: `git merge-file <ours> <old pristine> <new pristine>` per patched file, with the pristine crates from `~/.cargo/registry/src`. A file copied from there keeps its old modification time (PowerShell's `Copy-Item` too), and cargo then doesn't rebuild the vendored crate: touch what you copy, and check the build says `Compiling i-slint-core`.
- `fonts/vectorfont.rs` (`render_vector_glyph` + `text_tuning`): turns on TrueType **hinting** and a DirectWrite-style **enhanced contrast** curve (k=0.5) on glyph coverage. Without them, small Malgun Gothic text looked blurry and thin on dark backgrounds compared with native apps (compared at 3x zoom; k=0.75 looked too bold). `SIGWIN_HINT=0` / `SIGWIN_CONTRAST=<k>` override at runtime.

## `vendor/i-slint-core` (Slint 1.19.0)
- **Text styles** (Signal's bold/italic/strike/mono/spoiler `BodyRange`s): `styled_text.rs` adds `sigwin_styled` (StyledText from byte ranges, no markdown) and `sigwin_set_plain_style`, a registry by exact text that `shaping.rs` `create_text_paragraphs` applies to plain Text / read-only TextInput, so the selectable TextInput under the StyledText overlay gets the same font styles and both lay out identically (`gui::rows::to_item` registers, cleared on thread switch). `Style::Code` is plain monospace (no capsule, same size). Editable TextInputs skip that registry (a draft equal to a message must not take its styles) and use `sigwin_set_edit_styler` instead: multi-line ones (the composer) are styled by an app function called with the text as shaped, IME composition included, so the composer shows picked @mentions and text styles in place with dimmed markers (`gui::rows::sync_composer_styles`); single-line fields take no styles. A `Property` bumped on change invalidates the cached shaping. Upstream has no styled editing (slint-ui/slint#2723, #1325).
- **Spoilers**: `draw.rs`: a color with alpha 1 draws an opaque spoiler box of its RGB instead of the glyphs; spoilers are clickable via a links entry `sigwin-spoiler:<id>`.
- **Clickable links over selectable text**: `items/text.rs`: `StyledText` takes only mouse events over a link and ignores the rest, so a StyledText drawn over a transparent read-only TextInput gives clickable links (pointer cursor, `link-clicked`) while selection still works. Links are `SigwinStyle::Link` spans built in `gui::rows::rich_text`.
- **ListView end of model**: `model/repeater.rs` `update_visible_instances`: when the rows run out before the view is full ("Reached end of model with room to spare. Scroll up."), upstream raises `content_y_value` but not `new_offset_y`, which is what the next pass lays out from, so the rows stay where content-y put them, far above the view. Fixed, a content-y past the end lays out the last row at the bottom with real row heights above it in one pass; a model shorter than the view is kept at the top (row 0 clamped like a seek), or the rows would sit at the bottom with a positive content-y. `seek-end` relies on it: a switched-to thread at the bottom from its first frame, and the list kept at the bottom when the composer shrinks (without it the list went blank, and the software renderer panicked casting the far-off clip to i16). Upstream bug, still on master after 1.19.0; fix proposed in slint-ui/slint#14992. `ListView.ensure-row-visible(last, instant)` is no replacement: it puts a row taller than the view at its top, so a long last message showed its top first and slid down over a few frames.
- **CJK fallback**: `textlayout/sharedparley/shaping.rs`: the font stack is the requested family + `SIGWIN_CJK_FAMILIES` (Yu Gothic UI, Microsoft YaHei UI, Microsoft JhengHei UI) + generics. parley's script fallback picks one font per script, and for Han on Korean Windows that is Malgun Gothic again, which lacks Japanese/Chinese-only ideographs (駅 鉄 国 rendered blank). The fonts are memory-mapped and loaded only when a glyph needs them (no measurable memory cost).
